content: Granuloma faciale (GF) is a rare, non-cancerous, chronic skin condition of unknown cause. It is characterized by the presence of one or more skin nodules, which most commonly appear on the face. In some cases, lesions may also develop on other parts of the body, particularly in areas exposed to sunlight. The condition was first identified as a distinct medical entity in 1950 by Lever and Leeper. Later that same year, a group led by Pinkus proposed the term granuloma faciale to describe the disease. Granuloma faciale can resemble several other skin disorders, making accurate diagnosis challenging. Conditions that may be mistaken for GF include discoid lupus erythematosus, fixed drug eruption, mycosis fungoides, and sarcoidosis.
